reference.title: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Upper Arms, equipment Dumbbell, Bench, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2.3 s down

prescription.progression: Load is user-chosen: pick a dumbbell you can curl for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion); add reps, then weight. Start lighter than for the standing curl (clinical opinion).

cues.text: Set the back pad to about 45 degrees. Lie chest-down on it with the chin just over the top, feet on the floor behind, arms hanging straight down, palms forward.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells toward the shoulders; the upper arms stay vertical.
Squeeze at the top; chest stays on the pad.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows swinging forward as the weight rises
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms vertical; only the forearms move.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the chest off the pad
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest and hips against the pad.
Straighten the arms fully each rep.

mistakes.mistake: Craning the neck to look forward
mistakes.fix: Keep the head in line with the trunk, chin just over the pad.

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: The supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase; neutral grips shift work toward the brachioradialis (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Upper arms hang vertically, about 45 degrees of shoulder flexion relative to the trunk on a 45-degree pad; biceps activity peaked near 75 degrees of shoulder flexion in an isometric curl (Moon 2013)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)
Back pad about 45 degrees (common practice, clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Chest on the pad (skinned mesh gap)
kinematics.norm: Chest on the pad, chin over the top, feet planted behind (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #037412, Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl, video (movement reference)

Moon, Shin, Kang, Kim, Lee, Park, Kim, Hong, Koo and O'Sullivan 2013, the effect of shoulder flexion angles on the recruitment of upper-extremity muscles during isometric contraction (J Phys Ther Sci 25(10):1299-1301; PMC3820192)
Oliveira, Matta, Alves, Garcia and Vieira 2009, effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls (J Sports Sci Med 8(1):24-29; PMC3737788)
Coratella et al. 2023, biceps brachii and brachioradialis excitation in biceps curl exercise: different handgrips, different synergy (Sports 11(3):64; PMC10054060)

cautions: Elbow or shoulder pain: lighten the dumbbell and shorten the range; stop if pain is sharp (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight (in line with the forearm); a bent-back wrist under load strains the forearm (clinical opinion).
Pick the dumbbells up and set them down with a straight back and bent knees.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Pressure on the chest or breathing discomfort: set the pad a little steeper (clinical opinion).
modify: Shoulder or chest discomfort: steeper pad (55-60 degrees).
progressions: Slower lowering with a 1 s pause at the top.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Main elbow flexor; with the chest on the pad the arms hang straight down and the body cannot swing. With the arms hanging in front of the trunk (shoulder flexed), biceps activity rose with shoulder flexion up to about 75 degrees in an isometric curl (Moon 2013).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Main elbow flexor; with the chest on the pad the arms hang straight down and the body cannot swing. With the arms hanging in front of the trunk (shoulder flexed), biceps activity rose with shoulder flexion up to about 75 degrees in an isometric curl (Moon 2013).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) assists elbow flexion, most with the forearm near neutral.
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) assists elbow flexion, most with the forearm near neutral.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Wrist and finger flexors hold the handle and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Wrist and finger flexors hold the handle and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm vertical; it should not lift the elbows forward.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the upper arm vertical; it should not lift the elbows forward.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still so the hips do not swing the weight up.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades set on the pad.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades set on the pad.

phases.label: Chest on the pad, arms hanging

guides.label: Dumbbells curl up from straight below the shoulders
Elbow bends through a full range
